open_comment_speakers.name: Henry Vellandi
open_comment_speakers.topic: Neighborhood problems and possible resolution. A group consisting of neighbors, landlords and students/tenants working to bring viable solutions to Council.

open_comment_speakers.name: Maggie Lough
open_comment_speakers.topic: Also part of this working group to resolve issues with landlords, tenants and neighbors.

open_comment_speakers.name: Rudy Harberg
open_comment_speakers.topic: Spoke of the importance of partnership/dialogue between landlords/enforcement/tenants and neighbors in resolving “Hill” issues. Ratcheting up enforcement will not resolve the problems.

open_comment_speakers.name: Greg Sherwin
open_comment_speakers.topic: Landlord of rental houses on the Hill and in Goss Grove. Re: EEO Audit - concerned about the enforcement aspect focused on landlords without an enforcement mechanism for renters.

open_comment_speakers.name: Marty Crigler
open_comment_speakers.topic: Presented Council with the Goss Grove Neighborhood Association Position Statement on the 2/12/02 Council Study Session Agenda

open_comment_speakers.name: Doug Crigler
open_comment_speakers.topic: Member of Citizen Advisory Group which oversaw the EEO Audit. He stressed the importance of Council policy decisions.

open_comment_speakers.name: Michele Bishop
open_comment_speakers.topic: Addressed concerns regarding occupancy issues - urged that Council consider handout of questions as a starting point in this discussion.

open_comment_speakers.name: Rob Smoke
open_comment_speakers.topic: E-bikes - suggested that more information needs to be presented regarding potential benefits, particularly to physically challenged individuals.

open_comment_speakers.name: Brian Field
open_comment_speakers.topic: Landlord speaking to the difficult position landlords are in when faced with strict enforcement vs. providing affordable housing.

open_comment_speakers.name: Kirk Watson
open_comment_speakers.topic: demolition ordinance on first reading. While understanding the motivation of historic preservation, raised concern regarding practical impacts on an ageing housing stock in the city.

open_comment_speakers.name: Jeep Campbell
open_comment_speakers.topic: Subsidized housing issue - Again stressed the tax implications on the homes which are not being subsidized.

open_comment_speakers.name: Steven Wallace
open_comment_speakers.topic: Beverages Licensing Authority - spoke to role of the authority, understanding the benefit of the discussion but also stressed the value of neighborhood residents perspective.

open_comment_speakers.name: Lynn Segal
open_comment_speakers.topic: Concerns relating to the possible increase of 50,000 people to Boulder. This would be the equivalent of five Rock Creeks.

open_comment_speakers.name: Robert Sharpe
open_comment_speakers.topic: a progressive agenda for Transportation - in addition to more alternate modes, improve signs and road markings, improve driver education, and reinvigorate van pools and car pools.

open_comment_speakers.name: Ken Davies
open_comment_speakers.topic: On behalf of Villa de Prado Home Owner's Association - in favor of agenda item #13.

open_comment_speakers.name: Mark Fearer
open_comment_speakers.topic: Spoke about the efforts of the landlords, tenants and neighbors, to have calm discussions about issues.

motions.motion_text: Councilmember Corson moved, seconded by Ruzzin to approve Consent items 3A-3B.

Councilmember Morzel moved, seconded by Eldridge to introduce and order published by title only Ordinance No. 7182 amending Title 9, "Land Use Regulations," B.R.C. 1981, by making amendments to Section 9-1-3, "Definitions," amending the definitions of "Building Envelope" and "Setback," Section 9-1-4, "Financial Guarantees," Section 9-3.1-1, "Schedule of Permitted Uses of Land," Section 9-3.1-2, "Other Permitted Uses or Restrictions upon Land," Section 9-3.2-1, "Schedule of Bulk Requirements," Section 9-3.2-3, "Building Height," Section 9-3.2-13, "Setback Standards," Section 9-3.3-3, "Solar Access and Solar Siting and Construction," Section 9-3.4-12, "Accessory Dwelling Units," Section 9-3.4-13, "Owner's Accessory Unit," Section 9-3.4-17, "Antennae for Wireless Telecommunications Services," Section 9-3.4-18, "Cooperative Housing Units," Section 9-3.4-19, "Restaurants and Taverns," Section 9-3.6-2, "Variances and Interpretations," Section 9-4-8, "Development in Stages, Time of Approval, City Manager Review of Progress, and Expiration of Development Approval," Section 9-4-9 "Use Review," Section 9-4-11, "Site Review," Section 9-12-6, "Wetland Permit Application," and by the addition of a new appendix I, "Setback Averaging," and setting forth details in relation thereto.

Councilmember Morzel moved, seconded by Corson to introduce and order published by title only, Ordinance No. 7183 amending Chapter 10-13, “historic preservation,” B.R.C 1981, by amending the definition of “demolition”; by changing the standards for the demolition of buildings that are over fifty years old that are not individual landmarks or within historic districts; authorizing the creation of discontinuous historic districts; and authorizing the landmarks board design review committee to review plans for the construction of small structures in historic districts or in association with individual landmarks, as amended by the City Attorney.

Councilmember Mock moved, seconded by Morzel to introduce and order published by title only an Emergency Ordinance No. 7184 adopting Supplement No. 71 which codifies previously adopted Ordinance Nos. 7155, 7163, 7168, and 7169 as an amendment to the Boulder Revised Code 1981, and setting forth details in relation thereto.

Councilmember Mock moved, seconded by Havlick to introduce and order published by title only Ordinance No. 7185 to acknowledge the legal status of the subdivision Villa Del Prado PUD a 5.34 acre parcel property divided without the approval of a subdivision in the 1980's located at the southwest corner of the intersection of Baseline and Mohawk Drive.
BY MOTION REGULARLY ADOPTED, THE MEETING WAS ADJOURNED AT 9:56 P.M.
